At 9430s the speaker names an intermediary/junction table, at 9485–9535s draws two one-to-many relationships, and 9708–9800s maps class/student IDs into association rows. This supports f1 and offers a genuine whiteboard mechanism. But at 9807–9835s he says that if John drops out, foreign-key constraints 'get rid of these' association rows, without specifying a cascading delete policy. Foreign keys alone do not automatically delete children: PostgreSQL's approved constraint documentation distinguishes default NO ACTION from explicitly selected ON DELETE CASCADE. The supplied cut therefore teaches an unsupported automatic-cleanup rule. It also opens with 'implement that' and spends almost nine minutes on spelling, naming jokes and repetitive parent/child analogy. A replacement compact, standalone example must establish the M:N problem and two 1:M resolution without implying automatic deletion; simply retaining the supplied end preserves the accuracy defect.
